name: iOS Home Screen web apps
plain: On iPhone a site can only be installed by you from the Share menu, and some features work only after that.
meaning: iOS has no beforeinstallprompt, so a site cannot offer install. Web Push works only for a Home Screen app (iOS 16.4 and later). Installed apps are exempt from Safari's 7 day script storage cap.

web.api: Share > Add to Home Screen; navigator.standalone; matchMedia display-mode; PushManager (Home Screen apps only)

access.prompt_ui: Add to Home Screen sheet, started by you

safari.note: Add to Dock (17) on macOS; no beforeinstallprompt

ios_safari.note: Home Screen web apps get Web Push (16.4+) and are exempt from the 7 day storage cap

story.what_it_is: On iPhone, adding a site to the Home Screen unlocks push and longer storage.

marketing.name: Web Push for Web Apps on iOS and iPadOS
marketing.pitch: Home Screen web apps can receive push notifications on iOS 16.4 and later.

story.for_you: A site cannot pop up an install offer on iPhone. If you add it yourself, it can then ask to send notifications and keeps its data longer.
story.for_makers: Makers coach iPhone users through Share > Add to Home Screen before asking for push.

use_cases.example: A news site tells iPhone readers how to add it before asking for alerts.
A web chat app asks for push only inside the Home Screen app.

risks: Installed apps escape the storage cap that limits tracking in tabs
story.ios_note: This entry is about iOS. Safari on Mac has Add to Dock but no install prompt either.

technical_bounds: Web Push needs a Home Screen app on iOS 16.4+
